content: Metoprolol is a selective beta-1 receptor blocker that is commonly used in the treatment of various cardiovascular conditions, particularly hypertension. It is available in two forms: metoprolol succinate and metoprolol tartrate. Metoprolol tartrate is an immediate-release formulation, while metoprolol succinate is an extended-release formulation. A dose of 100 mg of metoprolol tartrate is equivalent to 95 mg of metoprolol succinate. Metoprolol is marketed under the brand names Lopressor® and Toprol XL®. Lopressor refers to the immediate-release metoprolol tartrate tablets, while Toprol XL refers to the extended-release metoprolol succinate tablets. This medication belongs to several therapeutic categories, including antianginal agents, antiarrhythmic agents, antihypertensive agents, antimigraine drugs, beta blockers, and cardiovascular drugs. The interaction between alcohol and metoprolol has not been definitively established. It is important to consult your doctor to understand the potential effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication.
